key_insight: Chemical composition and surface termination strongly control the band alignment at 2D/3D perovskite interfaces, making interface design a key lever for passivation and performance.
engineering_relevance: For perovskite solar cells, selecting the right 2D capping layer and 3D surface chemistry can tune work function and band offsets to improve stability and charge extraction.
method: Atomistic modeling of (PEA)2PbI4 / mixed-cation mixed-halide 3D interfaces
Consistent calculation of work function, electron affinity, and band offsets
evidence_signal: The abstract reports preliminary computed trends showing work function changes with cleavage/chemistry and band offsets spanning about 0.2–0.7 eV for valence and around 0.25 eV for conduction.
watch_item: Results are preliminary and may depend strongly on termination choice, so experimental validation and broader interface sampling are needed before design rules are generalized.
paper_title: Material chemical composition impacts on the band alignments: preliminary results on the 3D/2D perovskite interfaces
